column1: Who handles operating-system and database-engine patching for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column3: These managed services reduce infrastructure-maintenance work.

column1: What database-design work remains your responsibility in Azure SQL Database?
column2: Designing application objects such as tables, indexes, and constraints.
column3: Managed infrastructure does not replace application-specific database design.

column1: Which Azure SQL Database service tier separates compute from scalable storage for very large databases?
column3: Its architecture allows storage to grow independently of compute.

column1: How does Azure SQL Database Hyperscale scale out read workloads?
column3: Route suitable read workloads to replicas instead of the primary.

column1: Which Azure SQL Database compute tier automatically scales compute within configured limits as demand changes?
column3: The service adjusts compute rather than requiring each capacity change to be manual.

column1: What database resource remains billed while an Azure SQL Database serverless database is paused?
column3: Compute charges stop during the paused period.

column1: Why must applications use connection retries when accessing an automatically paused serverless database?
column2: Resuming the database can cause temporary connection failures.
column3: A retry allows the application to recover after the database resumes.

column1: Which Azure SQL Database feature can create workload-based indexes when its CREATE_INDEX option is enabled?
column3: It evaluates the effect of automatically applied index changes.

column1: How does automatic plan correction respond to a query-plan regression?
column2: It forces the last known good execution plan.
column3: This is a plan-selection action, not automatic index creation.

column1: Which Azure managed service targets near-complete SQL Server instance-level feature compatibility?
column3: Its compatibility reduces changes for many existing SQL Server applications.

column1: Which built-in service schedules database jobs in Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column3: Managed Instance supports instance-level job scheduling.

column1: What naming format references an object in another database on the same Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column3: Three-part names support cross-database queries within the instance.

column1: Which feature continuously replicates SQL Server data to Azure SQL Managed Instance for hybrid or migration use?
column3: It uses distributed availability groups for near-real-time replication.

column1: Which Azure SQL deployment option gives you direct control over the underlying operating system?
column2: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines.
column3: This option also gives control over the SQL Server installation and configuration.

column1: Which extension adds Azure portal management and backup or patching automation for SQL Server on Azure Windows VMs?
column3: Register the VM to access the extension's management features.

column1: What primary workload does SQL database in Microsoft Fabric serve?
column3: It is an operational database with built-in integration into Fabric analytics.

column1: Where does SQL database in Fabric automatically mirror supported operational tables for analytics?
column3: Mirroring avoids the need to build a separate extraction pipeline for those supported tables.

column1: Which Fabric SQL database endpoint provides read-only T-SQL access to mirrored analytical data?
column3: Read-only refers to table data, although the endpoint permits objects such as views.

column1: Which tool supports .bacpac import/export and .dacpac deployment operations for SQL database in Fabric?
column3: It supports database portability and changes to database object definitions.

column1: Who manages built-in high availability for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance?
column3: Unlike a self-managed SQL Server deployment, the service provides the availability infrastructure.
